Traditional Quebecois Tourtiere

Served at: Fourth Sunday of Advent

Serves 6-8Prep 30 minCook 1 hr 15 min

Tourtiere is a savory meat pie that holds a special place in Quebecois Christmas traditions, especially served on the Fourth Sunday of Advent. This hearty dish combines a blend of ground meats with warm spices, encased in a flaky pastry, symbolizing comfort and family togetherness during the holiday season.

Ingredients

  • 1 lb (450 g) ground pork
  • 1 lb (450 g) ground beef
  • 1 medium onion, finely chopped
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) beef broth
  • 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon
  • 1/4 tsp ground cloves
  • 1/4 tsp ground allspice
  • Salt and black pepper to taste
  • 1 tbsp (15 ml) vegetable oil
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) fresh parsley, chopped
  • 1 package refrigerated pie crusts (2 crusts) or homemade equivalent

Method

  1. Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
  2. In a large skillet, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and garlic, sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
  3. Add the ground pork and beef to the skillet. Cook until browned, breaking up the meat with a spoon, about 8-10 minutes.
  4. Drain excess fat if necessary. Stir in the beef broth, cinnamon, cloves, allspice, salt, and pepper. Simmer uncovered for 20 minutes until the mixture thickens slightly.
  5. Remove from heat and stir in the chopped parsley. Let the filling cool slightly.
  6. Roll out one pie crust and fit it into a 9-inch (23 cm) pie plate. Fill with the meat mixture, spreading evenly.
  7. Cover with the second pie crust. Trim excess dough and crimp edges to seal. Cut a few slits in the top crust to allow steam to escape.
  8. Bake in the preheated oven for 45 minutes or until the crust is golden brown.
  9. Let the tourtiere rest for 10 minutes before serving.

Tips

  • For a more traditional flavor, you can add a small amount of ground veal or wild game meat if available.
  • Serve with ketchup or a side of pickled beets for an authentic Quebecois experience.
  • Make the pie a day ahead to allow flavors to meld; reheat gently before serving.
